authorization: Mario requested a ChromaDB comparison after the SQLite and LanceDB tests

modes.native: Two independent SDK processes share the same synthetic local path; documentation does not support this as a safe deployment
modes.serialized-owner: Parent coordinator holds an OS file lock over each child SDK process's entire lifetime; child exits before lock release. No persistent server. All cooperating writers must use this path.

cases.expected: Raw original and provenance can be saved with no vector and no embedding function; rejection is a contract gap, not an infrastructure failure
All 60 observations survive with exact IDs/provenance; these Chroma storage fixtures carry explicit fixed vectors
One stored original after repeated add of the same identity
Two simultaneous attempts of the same operation leave one original
Two decisions based on revision 0 produce one accepted result and one detectable conflict. Native read-then-update has no atomic revision predicate; compare cooperative owner behavior separately.
A fresh reader process can retrieve another writer's confirmed record
SIGKILL after public batch-start notification preserves confirmed prefix and leaves batch absent or complete; no exact commit-phase injection
Fixed-vector nearest neighbor and document substring filtering honor project scope. Native missing-vector rejection is reported rather than replaced with a dummy vector.
Reusing operation or record identity with different immutable content is reported rather than silently treated as success
Invalid dimensions do not overwrite a previously stored vector/document; this is not raw-capture-without-embedding acceptance

comparison_limits: Original IDs/text/provenance and repetitions are reused. Except the explicit missing-embedding case, Chroma write fixtures include fixed [1,0,0] vectors because embedded collections may require embeddings; previous append fixtures had null vectors.
No model, automatic embedding, cloud endpoint or HTTP server
Native embedded multi-process results cannot override documented unsupported deployment constraints
Native Chroma document filtering is substring filtering, not FTS5/BM25; no claim of equivalent hybrid ranking
No public multi-table transaction or exact rollback boundary is assumed
No controlled timing, semantic-quality or classification benchmark
A cooperative owner serializes SDK lifetimes, not only add calls
